entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.

2. The present bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant in case crime No. 278 of 2021, under Sections-498A, 304B IPC and Sections-3 / 4 of D. P. Act, police station Lalganj, District Mirzapur, with the prayer to enlarge the applicant on bail.
3. It has been argued by learned counsel for the applicant that the applicant-accused is innocent and he has been falsely implicated in this case.
Applicant is husband of the deceased.
The marriage of deceased with applicant has taken place on 20.4.2015 and out of that marriage, they have two children.
Only general allegations of dowry demand and harassment of deceased have been levelled against all the accused persons, including the applicant.

It was submitted that as per prosecution Sanjay Kol vs State Of U.P. on 10 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40804611/
1 version, applicant used to consume liquor, due to which, deceased was not happy and in anger, she committed suicide by consuming some insecticide.

entities.text: Sanjay Kol vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the post mortem report, no injury has been shown on the body of the deceased and cause of death could not be ascertained, hence, viscera was preserved.
As per FSL report, aluminium phosphide has been found in viscera of the deceased.

It is further submitted that the alleged incident took place on 27.7.2021 and after that family members of deceased were informed and they were present at the time of inquest proceedings but at that time,
no complaint was made.
After about three months, on 20.10.2021 an application under Section 156 (3) CrPC was filed and thereafter this case has been registered on 11.11.2021.
The long delay in lodging the first information report creates a serious doubt about the authenticity of the prosecution version.
Lastly, it was submitted that the applicant is in jail since 5.8.2022, having no criminal history, and that in case applicant is enlarged on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.
4. Learned A.G.A. has opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that the applicant is husband of deceased who has suffered unnatural death within seven years of her marriage.

5. Considering the submissions of learned counsel for the parties and all attending facts and circumstances of the case, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the matter, a case for bail is made out.
Hence, the bail application is hereby allowed.

6. Let the applicant Sanjay Kol involved in the aforesaid crime be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two local sureties each of the like amount to the satisfaction of court concerned subject to the following conditions:
i. The applicant will not tamper with the evidence during trial.
ii.
The applicant will not pressurize/intimidate the prosecution witnesses.
iii. The applicant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.
iv. The applicant will not try to contact, threat or otherwise influence the complainant or any of the witness of the case.
7. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, the court concerned shall be at liberty to cancel the bail of applicant, in accordance with law.

Order Date :- 10.5.2024 HR  Sanjay Kol vs State Of U.P. on 10 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40804611/
